case_title: Rajinder Singh v. State of Haryana
statutory_provisions: IPC s.304-B, s.498-A and s.201 read with s.34; IPC s.201/34
aggravating_circumstances: Cremation hurried without informing parents, presence of pesticide in vomiting
trial_court_outcome: Convicted of husband u/ss 304-B, 498-A and 201 and of other accused u/s 201/34
high_court_outcome: Dismissed the appeals of the accused-appellants
neutral_facts: The accused, a man, married a woman, who later died under unusual circumstances. The woman was subjected to harassment by her husband and other relatives in connection with a dowry demand. The deceased's body was cremated shortly after her death without informing her parents. The forensic examination of the deceased's clothes and vomit revealed the presence of an organophosphorus pesticide. The prosecution argued that the death occurred under abnormal circumstances, within seven years of marriage, and that the accused failed to provide a satisfactory explanation for the hurried cremation and the presence of the pesticide. The trial court convicted the accused of dowry death, and the High Court upheld the conviction.
